industry.why: Neutral at industry level, carried, with the sector rows carrying the view: Utilities integrated moves to Overweight this week on the first European power-price reading in a month (Nordic power forwards up, Fortum's 22-year nuclear agreement with Google; Danske Bank, 28 October), Regulated networks stays Neutral and Renewable generators stays Underweight because the ten-year above 5% is the row's discount rate. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44). Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: D now, D prior, DISAGREES with the sector move; rate-sensitives lagged on the week (Outset Global). Counter-case for B: pricing-power defensives are the rotation's destination; for D: the tape. Moves to B if a second power-price reading arrives with the industry's relative strength leaving D.

sector.why: Neutral, carried. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): Jefferies' desk (17 Oct) names utilities among the 'pricing-power defensives' and utilities led the US week; against it, networks are the purest bond proxy, the Fed hikes in December, and no European power price or regulator decision was read. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: D now, C prior. Moves to B on a power-price reading in the sources or on the bond rally becoming a trend.

geography.why: Double Underweight, carried on a reading now three weeks stale, said plainly: the French premium (a record 150 basis points on 26 October) was not re-read; the one item this week is an undated headline that France's debt risks keep bond investors on edge (Investing Live), which agrees in direction and gives no level, so the conditions (to D under 120 basis points for a month; to C under 100) could not be tested. Component 1 regime, 13-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its 52-week high, still present on Richard's European test and weakening at the margin for the first time: breadth up a third week to 66%, 60%, 62% and 63% of stocks above the 50, 100, 150 and 200-day averages, the three longer ones still below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, cyclicals ahead of defensives over one week and twelve months while defensives lead at four weeks, three months and six months; the causes unread by any reasoned source for a second week, web headlines only, and the headlines lean against the rates squeeze of the 30-Oct-26 read: the Federal Reserve easing, oil below $100). 15 Pool stocks are French-listed. Counter-case: a top-letter country view held three weeks without a spread reading is the row most at risk of being simply out of date. Re-test when the premium is read; if it is unread for a fourth week the row goes to D on staleness alone.

experiment.label: Experiment
experiment.method: own daily moves (Stoxx Europe 600 and country-of-listing average removed), rank correlation, last 63 and 126 sessions; candidates EUR 500m or more in the same sector, cohort or country of listing

defs.atr: average true range: each day's high to low, stretched to the previous close on a gap, as a % of the previous close; L5D the last 5 sessions, L1M and L3M the last 30 and 91 calendar days
defs.top_half: a close above the midpoint of the day's high-low range; an up day closes at or above the previous close; days with no range are left out
